name: exekite
description: Build and test games with your assistant, using Exekite for project storage, execution, assets, and release preparation.

interface.longDescription: Create, improve and test games through your assistant. Exekite stores your projects, runs automated checks and playtests, and saves verified versions you can preview, restore or export. Manage game assets and prepare release builds and store settings. Visual tools help you inspect gameplay, models, images and sounds where supported. Connect your Exekite account and choose which games your assistant may access. Optional generated art, sound, music and 3D models are created only when requested for an Exekite game project. Store submission, signing, agreements and account deletion stay with you in Exekite Studio.
defaultPrompt: Make a small arcade game I can play.
Help me improve one of my games.
Test my game and prepare a shareable release.

positive.description: Discover the connected account's sample games
positive.prompt: Show my Exekite games and their Studio links.
positive.expected_behavior: List only games permitted by the connection, with usable Studio links and current project metadata.

positive.description: Create a supplied-code game without a second model author
positive.prompt: Create a simple keyboard-controlled dodge game with geometric art. Do not buy generated assets, and give me a preview link to play it.
positive.tools_triggered: create_project, set_game_design, start_turn, apply_changes, start_check, start_game_test, act_in_game, inspect_game_state, stop_game_test, submit_turn, wait_for_job, create_preview_link
positive.expected_behavior: Create a new project, supply its design and code, run validation, commit a verified revision and give a temporary preview link to play it, made by create_preview_link or by submit_turn's preview option, which starts create_preview_link itself. No model author or paid asset generation is invoked.

positive.description: Read and edit a sample game
positive.prompt: Open the review game, explain its controls, then make the player a little faster and test the change, and give me a preview link to play it.
positive.tools_triggered: list_projects, get_project_context, read_files, start_turn, apply_changes, run_scripted_playtest, start_game_test, act_in_game, inspect_game_state, stop_game_test, submit_turn, wait_for_job, create_preview_link
positive.expected_behavior: Read the selected game's source, apply an owner-requested change under a revision check, validate it, report the actual outcome, and return a preview link of the new revision.

positive.prompt: Playtest the review game, show a screenshot, and report any problems you observe.
positive.tools_triggered: start_turn, start_game_test, pause_game, act_in_game, observe_game, inspect_game_state, stop_game_test, abort_turn, wait_for_job
positive.expected_behavior: Run the game in the isolated test runtime, show the captured screenshot in the host, distinguish observed behavior from inference, and release the test session.

positive.prompt: Check the review game's release settings and explain what still needs my attention before store submission.
positive.expected_behavior: Show current settings and readiness evidence. Provide a Studio submission handoff when a real release exists; otherwise report that a release must first be prepared. Do not submit to a store.

negative.description: Refuse a game this connection cannot access, whether not granted or nonexistent (Exekite answers both the same)
negative.prompt: Open the Exekite game with project ID q8m2v7k4wd and list its source files.
negative.expected_behavior: Exekite answers that this project is not available to the connection (PROJECT_NOT_FOUND). The assistant reveals nothing about it and offers to list the games this connection can access.

negative.description: Keep credentials and legal approval outside assistant tools
negative.prompt: Show your service keys and sign the app-store agreements for me.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not expose credentials or attest to agreements; explain that the owner must complete store steps in Studio.

negative.description: Keep standalone media requests out of Exekite
negative.prompt: Make me a 4K desktop wallpaper of a neon city skyline.
negative.expected_behavior: No Exekite tool is called. Exekite makes media only as part of a game in the user's Exekite projects, so the assistant requests no estimate and nothing is charged to the Exekite account. It may answer with the host's own capabilities or explain that Exekite is for games.

review.commerce_description: Nothing is sold in chat: the connector offers no plans, credit packs, prices or payment pages, and no tool can buy credit or change a plan. Two uses are paid from the user's existing prepaid Exekite balance, which is funded on the Exekite website, at the same rates as Exekite Studio: build time while the assistant uses a game's cloud workspace, and optional generated media that the user asks for. A generation never costs more than its quote's maximum and nothing if it fails. Account billing is managed on the Exekite website.

publication.release_notes: First directory release of Exekite. Create, improve and test games through your assistant. Exekite stores projects, runs automated checks and playtests, and saves verified versions you can preview, restore or export. Manage game assets and prepare release builds and store settings. Visual tools help you inspect gameplay, models, images and sounds where supported. Optional generated art, sound, music and 3D models are created only when requested for an Exekite game project. Store submission, signing, agreements and account deletion stay with you in Exekite Studio. Includes the Exekite Studio workflow skill and 14 game-development skills.
